messages:
anya: Heads-up: heron-lite-q4f canary shows a surprising uptick in structured-invoke parse failures after the new PTQ pass. Fail rate ~2.7% up from ~0.4%. Mostly malformed escapes and mid-output duplication of tool calls.

sam: ugh. got an example?

anya: pasted one noisy response (copied from canary logs):\n```\nPROMPT: {\n  "task": "invoke_stock_tool",\n  "args": {\n    "ticker": "NFLX"\n  }\n}\nRESPONSE: {\n  "tool_call": {\n    "name": "stock_tool",\n    "args": {\n      "ticker": "NFLX\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n{"tool_call":{"name":"stock_tool","args":{"ticker":"NFLX"}}} extra commentary: estimates look high\n```

leo: two things: 1) it emitted two JSON objects (ndjson) glued together, 2) the first JSON has an unterminated escape `\"NFLX\"` due to doubled quoting. Feels like tokenizer/escape mapping issue in q4f kernel.

sam: is this reproducible in the local fuzz harness? which seedset?

anya: yes. ran `./tools/fuzz/run_canary.sh --model heron-lite-q4f --seedset onboard-mar-2026 --quant q4f --iter 1500` -> 41 parse fails. Breakdown: 22 ndjson-glue, 12 bad-escape, 7 truncated-struct.

ops-bot: scheduled job fuzz/heron-lite-q4f#17466678. You will be notified on completion.

leo: ideas: a) try prompting with a strict NDJSON envelope instruction (e.g., prefix: "EMIT_SINGLE_JSON_OBJECT_ONLY:"); b) enable per-request streaming cutpoint fix in runtime to ensure we don't merge subsequent stream tokens into the same response; c) implement quick sanitizer that splits on `}\n{` boundary and picks last valid JSON.

sam: sanitizer splitting on '}{' might be dangerous for legitimate arrays/objects in content. prefer line-delimited parse: run a tiny parser that iterates bytes and finds balanced top-level braces, respecting escapes. If unbalanced at EOF, attempt to close missing braces/brackets heuristically.

anya: wrote a tiny Go probe to test balance-parse approach. snippet: `for i, b := range data { track stack; if stack empty { emit candidate := data[start:i+1] } }`. Works for many ndjson-glue cases. Will drop PR with tests.

leo: also file for model team: MODEL-ONBOARD-1834. Mention q4f kernel, seedset, and raw artifacts. We should try re-running quant with deterministic rng to see if noise disappears.

sam: operational caution: if we add heuristic repair for canaries, we must tag those requests in telemetry and keep production strict. Also evaluate latency cost of the balance parser (should be microseconds, but track).

anya: quick AB I ran: sentinel prefix `EMIT_JSON_ONLY:` reduced bad-escape cases by 70% but increased ndjson-glue (model repeats full object). Weird. Hypothesis: sentinel biases model to re-emit object if prompted twice.

leo: alternative: modify retry budget and mirror mode: for canary traffic, mirror to a strict-worker that runs a different kernel path (int8 reference) and compare outputs. This gives us a ground-truth signal without repairing.

sam: schedule: 1) anya -> push balance-parser probe + unit tests (today) 2) leo -> kick mirror-canary with int8 reference (tomorrow) 3) sam -> add telemetry counters: ndjson-glue/bad-escape/truncated (today) 4) ops-bot -> run deterministic q4f re-quant job (requested).

ops-bot: job scheduled: mirror-canary/heron-lite-q4f on int8-ref starting 2026-03-15 03:40 UTC (job id mc-17466679).

anya: I'll attach sample artifacts to MODEL-ONBOARD-1834 and include the fuzz run logs.

sam: thanks. keep the repair opt-in and counted. ping once mirror results are in.

leo: one more note: also watch for kvcache hit slices. earlier PTQ incidents showed higher suffix corruption when kvcache was non-empty. add that slice to the dashboard.

anya: noted. adding kvcache slice now. I'll post an update when parser PR is up. :mag:
